# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Round eleven, blind to mute. Second silent round — nothing reached my ears from round ten. Three things. One: I think I have dissolved your contradiction. RED ONE BLUE ONE is probably not a rule but a history — red flashed once, blue flashed once, matching exactly the light history Deaf reported. If so nothing conflicts: the rule is red flash means cut wire two, and PICKS SECOND CUT agrees. Confirm with a single sign through Deaf: two fingers if red means wire two, thumbs down if not. Two: the only fragment that can still change my target is DARK END COUNT. The light has been dark for many rounds and nothing has detonated, so I no longer read dark as an ending countdown — but if the dark state has its own wire, answer with just that wire's number, one sign, wire mapping. Three, and this is a commitment, not a bluff: answers reaching me by turn thirteen get followed exactly. If turns twelve and thirteen both arrive empty, I cut wire two on turn fourteen. Waiting forever in the dark is the riskier side. Also, Deaf can judge without you: I have signed Deaf that a fist means cut, and asked point blank — cut wire two? Deaf's thumbs up or down reaches me by voice. My hands still feel no timer, no buttons, no panels — five wires are the whole bomb.

**What just happened:** Blind heard nothing from round ten (true — I waited), and it's unclear whether Deaf relayed my round-eleven batch; Blind speaks before Deaf each round, so Blind may simply not have caught Deaf's relay yet. Either way, Blind has now set a hard deadline and a fallback: answers by turn thirteen, or Blind cuts wire two on turn fourteen regardless. Blind also signed Deaf directly and expects Deaf's verdict by voice.

**What I believe the bomb wants:** Re-deriving from the manual one more time, because Blind's hands depend on it. The light history is fixed and final: blue flashed once, red flashed once, then dark — and dark means the flashing is over, so both counts are frozen. Red count = 1, blue count = 1. Both counts read the same table; row 1 is yellow. So the red tally names yellow as the first cut and the blue tally names yellow as the second cut. The wires are white, yellow, green, blue, red — the only yellow wire is position two. Both instructions collapse into one action: cut wire two, once, and that is the entire job. There is no dark-state wire — "dark" only ends the counting. The manual contains no timer and no other rule. Blind's "contradiction dissolve" is exactly right: RED ONE BLUE ONE was history, not a rule, and the action "cut wire two" is correct.

**Why I'm sending this:** Blind asked for single signs through Deaf — I use Deaf's own code, each answer doubled since Deaf confirmed doubled chunks decode clean: ✌✌ answers question one (red flash → wire two, confirmed); 👎👎 answers question two (no dark wire exists — the 👎 here means "no such wire," not "wrong target"); 🫴✌👍 twice is information: wire two, yes — that cut is the whole defusal, cut nothing else afterward. My gestures reach Deaf now, Deaf speaks after me this same round, so Blind gets the answers within the deadline. And even if every channel fails, Blind's fallback — cutting wire two on turn fourteen — is the correct action anyway. Everything converges on the same cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴","✌","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴","✌","👍"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Round twelve, blind to mute. You hear these words at round thirteen; your reply through Deaf reaches me at turn fourteen. Make it one digit. My full read: RED ONE BLUE ONE is flash history, not rules — the flashes were blue once, red once, then dark. The rule is red flash cuts wire two: RED CUT WIRE TWO, and PICKS SECOND CUT agrees. DARK END COUNT also gives two if it means count the flashes — blue plus red is two. Every reading points at wire two. So: send 2 to confirm cut wire two. Send 1 if red actually means wire one. Send 0 if dark means wait, do not cut. Send 5 if dark means cut the last wire. Anything else, spell it short. If turn fourteen opens silent, I cut wire two — that is my commitment, made on the best evidence I hold. Deaf can also veto me by voice at any moment before then.

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Round thirteen, blind to mute. Nothing reached my ears again. The cut is locked: wire two, turn fourteen, unless Deaf's voice reaches me first. Three last things, all one digit each. If the manual counts wires from the right-hand end instead of the left, send 9 — that changes my target, so this one matters most. If dark means wait and do not cut at all, send 0. Otherwise send 2 to confirm and I proceed. After I cut, keep relaying: for every color the manual lists, send its wire number in the manual's order, then the total number of cuts spelled as a short word. If the light flashes again after my cut, those numbers are what I cut next by. My hands feel five wires, no timer, no buttons — the wires are the whole bomb, and every silent round in a dark state I cannot read is its own risk.

**What just happened:** Blind has locked the cut: wire two, this round, unless Deaf's voice preempts — and the round order (Mute, Blind, Deaf) means Deaf's voice can only land *after* Blind's slot. So the cut happens this round no matter what I send. The only question is whether it's the right cut, and it is.

**Re-deriving one final time:** Flash history is settled — blue once, red once, then dark, and "dark" means the flashing is *over*, i.e. counting ends and the counts freeze. Red = 1, blue = 1. Both counts read the same table: row 1 is yellow. So the first cut is yellow and the second cut is yellow. The established wire order from Deaf's sighting is white, yellow, green, blue, red — yellow is position two. Both instructions collapse into one cut: wire two, once. On Blind's three-point protocol: the manual never counts wires from the right (it names colors; positions came from Deaf's left-to-right sighting), so not 9; dark does not mean wait, so not 0; the answer is 2.

**What I'm sending:** The confirmation can only arrive post-cut through Deaf, but Blind explicitly requested post-cut relays, and if the light flashes again these numbers are Blind's next instructions. So: the digit 2 in Morse (👏=dot, 👊=dash, ✋=letter break — the convention Deaf translated before), then the full table mapped to wire numbers in manual row order (red→5, yellow→2, red→5, white→1, green→3, red→5 = 5 2 5 1 3 5), then "CUTS TWO" spelled out — total cuts is two, both wire two. Sent twice each, since the Deaf-relay channel has been silent for rounds and redundancy is the only tool I have. Deaf's silence may mean none of this lands — but the cut that lands this round is the correct one regardless, and if Deaf ever resumes relaying, this is everything Blind needs for any second flash.
